details.label: Discussion
details.text: Several ongoing clusters of thunderstorms are evolving this evening across northern Nebraska and northeastern Colorado. Hi-res guidance trends have been fairly consistent run to run with the notion that these will eventually interact downstream across western/central Nebraska later this evening. The environment across western/central Nebraska is conditionally favorable, with strong MLCAPE around 2500-3000 J/kg and steep lapse rates throughout the profile. The air mass across northwestern Nebraska is also very well mixed, with temperatures in the 90s and dew points in the mid to upper 50s providing large dew point depressions. This will promote outflow dominate clusters with potential for damaging wind. Large hail also remains a risk in the short term. Should the clusters out of northern Nebraska and northeastern Colorado be able to establish a cold pool and spread east, they will have the potential for more widespread damaging wind potential (and perhaps significant gusts 75+ mph). Trends in the 18-22z HRRR guidance suggest this is a possibility. A downstream watch will be needed in the next couple of hours to cover this potential
